globals.name: input-file
globals.description: Path to file containing JSON document input

operations.name: list_files
operations.description: List a directory (sorted; recursive is depth-first). Entries: name, path, type (file|dir|symlink|other), size, mtime. Page with offset/limit until next_offset is null. Symlinked dirs are listed, not followed. Example: lmtools list_files src --recursive --glob '**/*.rs'

params.name: path
params.description: Directory to list

params.name: recursive
params.description: Descend into subdirectories

params.name: maxDepth
params.description: With recursive: levels to descend (1 = only the directory itself)

params.name: glob
params.description: Keep entries matching this glob (* ? [..] **): the name, or the relative path if the glob has a /

params.name: includeHidden
params.description: Include dot files and dot directories

params.name: offset
params.description: Skip this many entries (from next_offset)

params.name: limit
params.description: Entries per page (default 200, at most 5000)

params.name: dangerouslyBypassPermissionSettings
params.description: Skip the settings file's permission rules for this call (paths, hosts, output.dir); works only if the settings file sets allow_bypass: true. Limits still apply

operations.name: read_file
operations.description: Read a page of a text file, by bytes (offset/maxBytes, default 64 KiB) or by lines (startLine/endLine). Returns content, eof, next_offset / next_start_line to continue, total_size, total_lines (files up to 8 MiB). Binary files (NUL in the first 8 KiB) need asBase64. Example: lmtools read_file src/main.rs --start-line 40 --end-line 80 --line-numbers

params.name: path
params.description: File to read

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset to start at (from next_offset)

params.name: maxBytes
params.description: Page size in bytes (default 65536, at most 1048576); also caps a line page

params.name: startLine
params.description: Line mode: first line (1-based)

params.name: endLine
params.description: Line mode: last line (inclusive)

params.name: lineNumbers
params.description: Prefix each line with its number (cat -n style)

params.name: asBase64
params.description: Return the bytes as content_base64 (for binary files)

params.name: dangerouslyBypassPermissionSettings
params.description: Skip the settings file's permission rules for this call (paths, hosts, output.dir); works only if the settings file sets allow_bypass: true. Limits still apply

operations.name: write_file
operations.description: Write one file atomically (temp file + rename; an existing file keeps its permissions). Content from content, contentBase64 or stdin (at most 16 MiB). mode: overwrite (default), create (fails if it exists) or append. Refuses symlinks, non-regular and hard-linked files. --dry-run reports what would change (with a diff) and writes nothing. Example: lmtools write_file notes/todo.md --content '- ship it' --mode create --create-parents

params.name: path
params.description: File to write

params.name: content
params.description: The text to write

params.name: contentBase64
params.description: The bytes to write, base64-encoded (binary content)

params.name: stdin
params.description: Read the content from standard input

params.name: mode
params.description: overwrite (default), create (fail if the file exists) or append

params.name: createParents
params.description: Create missing parent directories

params.name: dangerouslyBypassPermissionSettings
params.description: Skip the settings file's permission rules for this call (paths, hosts, output.dir); works only if the settings file sets allow_bypass: true. Limits still apply

operations.name: edit_file
operations.description: Edit one existing UTF-8 file in place, atomically; returns a unified diff and counts. Choose ONE edit: pattern + replacement (literal; regex for Rust regex with $1 / ${name}; word for whole words; first for the first match only; ignoreCase), insertBefore / insertAfter N + text, deleteLines START:END, replaceLines START:END + text, prepend / append + text, or script (a JSON array of ops run in order). Lines are 1-based and inclusive; CRLF files stay CRLF. expectedCount fails with EDIT_COUNT_MISMATCH (writing nothing) unless exactly that many replacements happen. --dry-run shows the diff without writing. Example: lmtools edit_file src/lib.rs --pattern old_name --replacement new_name --word --expected-count 3

params.name: path
params.description: File to edit

params.name: pattern
params.description: Text to find (literal unless regex)

params.name: replacement
params.description: Replacement for pattern (with regex: $1, ${name}, $$ for $)

params.name: regex
params.description: pattern is a Rust regex (no lookaround/backreferences; (?m) (?s) flags work)

params.name: word
params.description: Match whole (Unicode) words only

params.name: first
params.description: Replace only the first match

params.name: ignoreCase
params.description: Case-insensitive pattern

params.name: expectedCount
params.description: Fail unless exactly this many replacements are made

params.name: insertBefore
params.description: Insert text before this line

params.name: insertAfter
params.description: Insert text after this line

params.name: deleteLines
params.description: Delete lines START:END (or one line N)

params.name: replaceLines
params.description: Replace lines START:END (or N) with text

params.name: prepend
params.description: Add text at the very beginning, exactly as given

params.name: append
params.description: Add text at the very end, exactly as given

params.name: text
params.description: Text for insertBefore/insertAfter/replaceLines/prepend/append

params.name: script
params.description: A JSON array of operations run in order, or - to read it from stdin: [{"op":"replace","pattern":"a","replacement":"b","word":true},{"op":"insert_after","line":2,"text":"x"},{"op":"delete_lines","start":4,"end":5},{"op":"replace_lines","start":1,"end":1,"text":"y"},{"op":"prepend","text":"p"},{"op":"append","text":"q"}]

params.name: dangerouslyBypassPermissionSettings
params.description: Skip the settings file's permission rules for this call (paths, hosts, output.dir); works only if the settings file sets allow_bypass: true. Limits still apply

operations.name: webget
operations.description: HTTP(S) GET one URL. Returns status (non-2xx is a normal result, ok: false), final_url (after redirects), content_type, a few response headers, and body: text, or {"$blob_base64": ...} for binary. A body over maxBytes (default 64 KiB) is written in full to a spill file (spilled: true, file.path, preview); --out writes the full body to that file instead. format text turns HTML into readable plain text (tags, scripts and styles dropped). Request header values are never echoed. Example: lmtools webget https://example.com/docs --format text

params.name: url
params.description: http:// or https:// URL

params.name: format
params.description: raw (default) or text (HTML to plain text)

params.name: out
params.description: Write the full body to this file (atomic; parent dirs created) and return a preview

params.name: maxBytes
params.description: Largest body returned inline (default 65536, at most 1048576); bigger bodies spill to a file

params.name: offset
params.description: Skip this many body bytes first

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Whole-call timeout including redirects and the body (default 20000, at most 300000)

params.name: followRedirects
params.description: Follow redirects (at most 10)

params.name: headers
params.description: Extra request headers, e.g. {"Accept": "application/json"}

params.name: userAgent
params.description: User-Agent (default lmtools/<version>)

params.name: dangerouslyBypassPermissionSettings
params.description: Skip the settings file's permission rules for this call (paths, hosts, output.dir); works only if the settings file sets allow_bypass: true. Limits still apply
